rows.name: Asia Fest (Year of the Fire Goat Lunar New Year celebration)
rows.schedule_text: February 12-13, 2027 at the Navy Exchange Mall, Salt Lake, per the organizer's page. Hours not stated.
rows.description: Lunar New Year celebration for the Year of the Fire Goat, billed by the organizer as one of Hawaii's largest. The 2026 edition (Explore Asia Fest) had Korean, Filipino and Japanese hot food, packaged food, snacks and drinks, retailers, entertainment and a petting zoo. The 2027 vendor mix is not stated.
rows.notes: Organizer page lists Feb 12-13, 2027 and the Navy Exchange Mall, Salt Lake, with no street address or hours. The page itself is undated, so it is not clearly current; medium until the organizer posts details. The 2026 Explore Asia Fest was Feb 28, 2026, 10 a.m.-7 p.m., free, at Palama Settlement, 810 N. Vineyard Blvd (HNN 2026-02-23 and KHON2). Same organizer, different venue and name, so likely the same series. The Instagram handle @pacificexpohawaii comes from the KHON2 event listing and was not seen on the organizer's own page. Organizer phone given by KHON2 for the 2026 event: 808-732-6037. Side 'town' is my placement of Salt Lake in the urban Honolulu area. 2027 admission not stated.

rows.name: Eggs Hawaii / Ka Lei Eggs
rows.address: 419 Waiakamilo Rd, Unit E1, Honolulu, HI 96817
rows.organizer: Eggs Hawaii (Ka Lei Eggs / Hawaiian Maid Eggs)
rows.description: Staffed retail store selling Ka Lei and Hawaiian Maid Island Fresh Eggs from the company's own page. Not a roadside or honor stand.
rows.notes: The company's contact page names the retail store 'Eggs Hawaii Inc - Island Fresh Eggs' at 419 Waiakamilo Rd (listed as Unit 1E in one place and Unit E1 in another), phone (808) 841-7695. This ties the Star-Advertiser 'Island Fresh Eggs' shop to this business. The company office is at 1590 Hau Street, phone (808) 841-7521. The Facebook page is the business's own. Current hours are not stated on any own page I could read. An older Honolulu Magazine item gave 8:30-3:30 Mon-Fri and 7:30-2 Sat, but it is several years old and directory hours conflict, so schedule_text is null. Honolulu Magazine's March 2025 update still lists the shop at this address. No 2026 own post found, so still_active is null rather than true. Ka Lei eggs are also sold at Kakaʻako Farmers Market (already in the directory).

rows.name: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (Kimchi Day Festival)
rows.schedule_text: Annual one-day festival; 2026 edition Saturday, November 14, 2026, 10 AM-7 PM.
rows.organizer: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (earlier editions hosted by The United Korean Association of Hawaii)
rows.description: A day of kimchi, cultural performances and community activities, per the organizer. The Hawaii Parent November 2026 calendar adds kimchi tastings and food vendors.
rows.notes: Organizer's own page confirms the 2026 date and hours (current, 14 days out). Hawaii Parent's November 2026 calendar matches. The organizer page does not state a 2026 venue. Earlier editions were at Makiki District Park Field, 1527 Keeaumoku St: the 2024 edition per the organizer page and KHON2, and a 2025 edition per Honolulu Magazine. Venue, neighborhood and side are left null until the organizer states it. Free admission was reported by KHON2 for the 2024 edition only. Instagram/Facebook handles not captured.

rows.name: Oahu Fresh (Farmers' Market Box / subscription delivery)
rows.schedule_text: Weekly or biweekly produce bag delivery or pickup at various island pickup locations; the site mentions weekly Wednesday delivery in one member comment. Order cutoffs apply each week.
rows.admission: Farmers' Market Box $25 plus a delivery fee, per the company's shop page. A $15 membership fee is cited by Slow Food Oahu and older company pages, not on the current shop page seen.
rows.description: Subscription and online produce service delivering since 2009. The Farmers' Market Box is a curated bag of 6-7 fruits and vegetables that varies weekly. It also offers a Make Your Own box ($30) and a Fruit Box ($40).
rows.notes: The live shop page shows current products and prices but is undated. The company's about page lists delivery charges by region (Region 1 $2.50 plus tax, Region 2 $5), but it is an archive page and may be dated. Delivery or pickup options are not captured here. It is a delivery subscription, not a market, so no directory kind fits and kind is null. Weekly bag contents are announced each Monday per Slow Food Oahu. The company runs from the Oahu Food Hub, 916 Kaaahi Place (per a farm directory; not used as a venue). Old press fees: Star-Advertiser 2020 gave a $15 membership and $5-7 delivery. No 2026 post found.

rows.name: Okinawan FEASTival
rows.venue_name: Okinawan-owned restaurants and food businesses across Oʻahu
rows.schedule_text: Annual two-week run of restaurant specials after the Okinawan Festival. The 7th FEASTival ran September 7-21, 2026 (range). The 2027 run has not been announced.
rows.description: Dining promotion in which Okinawan-owned and Okinawan-at-heart restaurants and food businesses on Oʻahu offer Okinawan-inspired specials.
rows.source_label: Organizer website (FEASTival Specials page) plus Star-Advertiser 2026-09-02
rows.notes: The 2026 run has ended (Sept 21). The two date entries are the start and end of a continuous range, not two separate events. Organizer specials page is titled for the 7th FEASTival, Sept 7-21, 2026; Star-Advertiser (2026-09-02) says the seventh annual run was Sept 7-21 with the full participant list at hawaiiokinawans.com. Honolulu Magazine says 20 restaurants took part. Examples in 2026 coverage: Oide Kitchen (212 Merchant St), Masa & Joyce (Kāneʻohe), Sunrise Restaurant (525 Kapahulu Ave), SKY Waikiki, an Aloha Andagi pop-up at Marukai Dillingham, and Beer Lab Pearlridge. The specials page also carries leftover entries from an earlier edition (for example a Saturday 9/13 sale at Ige's Halawa, which fits 2025, not 2026). I could not verify the conflicting 'November 2 - 8' line from my results, so I treat it as a leftover. The Okinawan Festival itself was Sept 5-6, 2026 at the Hawaii Convention Center. The Facebook page is the festival's, which mentions the FEASTival. still_active is true because the organizer ran the 2026 program and the series is annual.

rows.name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (farm stand)
rows.description: Cage-free egg farm on Oʻahu's North Shore (also called Villa Rose Egg Farm). Its sales are mainly to retailers, and a public farm stand is not confirmed in the sources I could use.
rows.notes: Sells eggs, not fruit. The farm itself is operating: WATTAgNet (about Aug 2025) reports four new barns under construction, and Civil Beat (2023) reports an active farm. Its own pages describe the farm and brand and do not give stand hours or an address. Stand address and hours appear only on review/map directories, which I excluded, so both are null. Whether the public stand is still open is not confirmed, so still_active is null (farm operating, stand unconfirmed). The farm is jointly owned by Hidden Villa Ranch and Rose Acre Farms (Civil Beat). The earlier-found Facebook page was not re-verified.

rows.name: Asagi Hatchery (fresh eggs and produce storefront)
rows.schedule_text: The hatchery's own contact page lists store hours of Monday to Friday 8am-5pm and Saturday 9am-noon.
rows.description: Family-owned hatchery in Kalihi hatching chicks since 1935. It sells hatching eggs, chicks, chicken supplies and feed, and fruit trees. Fresh eggs and produce for sale are not currently confirmed.
rows.notes: Primarily a hatchery and supply store, so it is a stretch as an egg stand. The home page address is 1830 Kanakanui Street, and the site shows a fruit-tree availability list dated 2026, so the website is maintained. It asks customers to call (808-845-4522) before visiting for trees. Contact-page hours are undated, and non-review directories give different hours (for example Mon-Fri 9-3), so confirm by phone. A hawaiianlocal.com listing, which seems to repeat the Facebook text, says it sold fresh eggs from Peterson Upland Farm; the user note says that farm closed in 2024 (Honolulu Magazine), so egg sourcing may have changed. The Facebook page is the business's own. An Instagram handle (@asagihatchery) appears on a farm-directory listing but was not seen on the business's own pages, so it is left null.

rows.name: De La Mesa Farms CSA boxes
rows.schedule_text: Historically CSA boxes with pickup locations on the Windward side and in Honolulu (listed in 2020). The farm has since relocated to Washington State.
rows.description: Former Waimānalo farm (Bryan and Natalie Mesa) that sold microgreens, produce, salsa and CSA boxes on Oʻahu before moving to Tacoma, WA.
rows.notes: No longer an Oʻahu operation, so likely not listable. GoFarm Hawaii's Windward profile lists De La Mesa Farms as 'online (re-located to WA)'. A Land Conservation Assistance Network entry says the owners began in Waimānalo and bought 2.5 acres in Tacoma in 2020, and the farm's own site (delamesafarms.com) and a South Sound Magazine feature describe a Tacoma farm and CSA. The Sierra Club Oʻahu list that supplied the original row is a pandemic-era resource page. The handle @delamesahawaii and the delamesahawaii.com website are tied to this farm by GoFarm Hawaii's 2018 farmer profile (website and Instagram/Facebook). The delamesahawaii.com site was not re-checked as live, and the handle may be dormant. A Forbes 2019 profile also describes an Oʻahu CSA and Kakaʻako/Kailua market booths, which are historical.

rows.name: Ewa Orchid Society Orchid Show and Plant Sale
rows.schedule_text: Annual show. The 2026 show (76th annual) was Friday July 17 and Saturday July 18, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
rows.description: 76th annual orchid show and plant sale with the theme 'Christmas in July' (Honolulu Orchid Society listing). Judging was held the evening of July 16.
rows.source_label: American Orchid Society event calendar, corroborated by the Honolulu Orchid Society event listing
rows.notes: This event has already happened. Venue, address and times come from the American Orchid Society calendar; the Honolulu Orchid Society listing gives July 17 9:00 am to July 18 4:00 pm and names the Ewa Elementary School Cafeteria. Per-day 9-4 hours follow the AOS show times, so verify. Both sources are third-party; the Ewa Orchid Society's own site or social page was not found, so confidence stays medium. Admission not stated. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found. still_active is true because the society held its 76th annual show in July 2026.

rows.name: Haleiwa Town Festival
rows.schedule_text: Listed for Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9 AM to 2 PM.
rows.description: One-day North Shore festival with local artists, merchants, food vendors and entertainers, per an events aggregator.
rows.source_label: Events aggregator (Best of Oahu, November 2026 calendar)
rows.notes: Single aggregator source, and no organizer page was found. The aggregator gives the location as Waialua Community Association, the same venue it gives for a separate Haleiwa Town Art Walk on Nov 7. That does not obviously fit a Haleʻiwa town street festival, so the venue and the street setting are unverified, and the venue_name and times may be copy-forward errors. A different event on the same day is Holoholo to Haleʻiwa, 2-4 PM at the Kamehamalu Courtyard (Haleʻiwa Store Lots); it is not this festival. The Haleiwa Arts Festival (June) and the July 4 festival are separate events. Confirm with the organizer before listing. Admission and hours come from the aggregator only.
